sample_unit: real-world emergency department notes (blinded physician evaluation)

links.outcome: Top-3 diagnostic accuracy with evidence-grounded verification framework versus standalone LLM on case reports
links.effect: Top-3 accuracy 59.9% vs 52.1% (JAMA) and 62.7% vs 51.4% (NEJM); Annals of Emergency Medicine 85.7% vs 68.6%.
links.quote: On literature-derived case reports from NEJM and JAMA, with GPT-oss-120B as the shared backbone, Top-3 diagnostic accuracy was 59.9% versus 52.1% for the standalone LLM on JAMA cases and 62.7% versus 51.4% on NEJM cases.

links.outcome: Capture of physician-consensus must-not-miss diagnoses in top three differential
links.effect: AegisDx captured at least one must-not-miss condition in top three in 78.0% of cases versus 52.0% for standalone LLM.
links.quote: against physician-consensus must-not-miss diagnosis sets, AegisDx captured at least one such condition among its top three diagnoses in 78.0% of cases versus 52.0%.

unlisted_practices: Multi-component LLM diagnostic framework with explicit must-not-miss screening and verification gates

screen.reason: Evaluates a safety-oriented framework (AegisDx) incorporating verification gates, explicit must-not-miss condition screening, and evidence retrieval added to an LLM backbone compared against standalone LLM baselines.

primary.practice: safety verification gates and must-not-miss screening guardrails
